note: Machine-readable registry of POD Go rules and non-schema-expressible knowledge. This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the verified/unverified status of each fact; docs/presets/business-rules.md renders it and docs/knowledge/verified.md presents the status split. 'demonstrated_by' lists preset(s) that prove the rule (see data-presets/demonstrations/manifest.json). A rule id used as a 'rule' in that manifest MUST appear here.

status_model.verified: Jointly confirmed with the project owner AND has an accompanying demonstrator preset. For viability facts the demonstrator must be hardware-confirmed. Never set from analysis alone.
status_model.unverified: The honest default: presumed/expected (research, inference, Line 6 sources), or not yet jointly confirmed. Everything starts here.

rules.statement: free_blocks = (number of blockN slots) - (number of built-in blocks present); base is 10 slots.
rules.rationale: The intuitive '7 - Vol - Wah - FX Loop' rule is wrong; it only coincidentally matches presets that keep EQ+Amp+Cab. Count slots minus built-ins.

rules.statement: The assignable ceiling is 7 free blocks; keeping Volume or the FX Loop while showing 7 free produces a phantom slot the UI won't assign.
rules.rationale: POD Go displays free blocks beyond the ceiling but won't let you assign them, so the preset reads as broken.

rules.statement: A genuine 7 free blocks requires removing BOTH Volume and FX Loop (Wah also costs a slot).
rules.rationale: Consequence of the 7 assignable-block ceiling: any built-in kept while at 7 free yields a phantom slot.

rules.statement: Keep the Amp block; removing it tends to break the preset. Removing only the Cab (keeping the Amp) is fine.
rules.rationale: Every no-amp / no-amp-and-cab preset in the library is broken; every no-cab preset works.

rules.statement: Removing both Amp and Cab collapses the chain to 8-9 blockN slots (vs the healthy 10) and reliably breaks.
rules.rationale: Strong evidence that removing both destabilizes the chain; every known example is broken.

rules.statement: At least one of EQ or Looper must remain in a preset (the mandatory block; EQ is convertible to Looper).
rules.rationale: Design constraint of the block chain.

rules.statement: The Cab block is single-cab only; POD Go does NOT support Helix's dual-cab mode.
rules.rationale: A research draft claimed dual-cab; the unit corrected it (project owner).

rules.statement: A preset can carry a duplicate built-in block (e.g. two Volume blocks) - a plausible cause of breakage.
rules.rationale: Surfaced by classifying presets by content; the duplicate coincides with a broken status.

rules.statement: A free/empty block is exactly {"@position": N}; a healthy preset exposes 10 blockN slots (block0-block9).
rules.rationale: Occupied blocks add @model + params; the bare @position form is the assignable slot.

rules.statement: A missing blockN slot (fewer than 10) silently lowers the free-block count below the intended value.
rules.rationale: An accidental slot drop during editing changes the count with no error.

rules.statement: @type by built-in role (factory): Volume 0, Wah 0, FX Loop 5, EQ(_STATIC) 0, Looper 4, Amp 1, Cab 2. Some Delay/Reverb free blocks are type 5.
snapshot0-3, footswitch, and controller sections carry per-snapshot block on/off, footswitch labels/leds, and parameter controllers (@controller 3..8).
rules.rationale: The structure of the assignment sections; these are the keys a blank-slate strip removes.

rules.statement: The built-in preset-EQ uses HD2_EQ_STATIC_* (matches the eq built-in prefix HD2_EQ_); free-block EQ effects use HD2_EQ* WITHOUT the underscore and are not built-ins. The same models exist in both forms and can coexist in one preset.
rules.rationale: Only the _STATIC_ form is the dedicated preset-EQ slot; the rest are free effects.

rules.statement: meta.name is hard-capped at 16 characters; a hand-edited over-length name is silently truncated to 16 on import (not rejected).
rules.rationale: POD Go Edit will not type past 16; the screen shows all 16.

rules.statement: A forward slash in meta.name is stored on disk escaped as \/ (an optional JSON escape decoding back to /). Spaces and symbols are allowed in names.
rules.rationale: Byte-for-byte match to POD Go's serialization requires writing \/ ; a bare / parses but won't match the device output.

rules.statement: The .pgp filename is decoupled from the stored name: export sanitizes / to _ in the filename, and import reads meta.name and ignores the filename.
rules.rationale: Renaming the file on disk has no effect on the loaded preset name.

rules.statement: Never reformat a .pgp file. Preserve POD Go's exact bytes: it escapes / as \/ and tolerates a trailing comma that strict parsers reject.
rules.rationale: A JSON re-serializer normalizes \/ to / and strips trailing commas, producing noisy, meaningless diffs. .pgp files are in .prettierignore.

rules.statement: POD Go tolerates a trailing comma that makes the file invalid to strict JSON parsers; the tools recover and flag it (parse: recovered-trailing-comma).
rules.rationale: At least one hand-edited preset has a trailing comma the device accepts.

rules.statement: Publish a blank slate: no loaded effects in free blocks, no footswitch/controller assignments. snapshot0-3, footswitch, and controllers are safe to delete - POD Go rebuilds them.
rules.rationale: Intended published state; the device reconstructs the deleted sections on import/first assignment.
